name: Toronto
tagline: Canada's big, multicultural city on the lake
summary: Canada's largest city sits on Lake Ontario, with the CN Tower over a skyline of glass towers. Half its people were born abroad, so its neighbourhoods and food come from all over the world, and Niagara Falls is an easy day trip.
seasonNote: June to September is warm, with festivals almost every weekend, including the film festival (TIFF) in September. October brings autumn colours. Winters are cold and snowy, from December to March.
arrival: Pearson Airport is 25 minutes from Union Station on the UP Express train. Billy Bishop Airport on the islands has flights from nearby cities, and trains run from Montreal (about 5 hours).
gettingAround: The TTC subway, streetcars and buses use one fare with a Presto card or a tap of your bank card; ferries cross to the islands.
cashTip: Cards and tap payments work everywhere; tip 15 to 20 percent in restaurants.
foodTip: Peameal bacon sandwiches, butter tarts, Caribbean roti and dim sum, plus food from almost every country.
buyTip: Maple syrup, Canadian whisky, Indigenous art and ice wine.
baseArea: Downtown near Union Station, or the Annex
